mainTopic: Short-lived creatures, extra organs and טרפה, a bird's down, and animals that ate harmful things
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about small boneless creatures. Dates stored in a jar for twelve months are permitted, and רב says a mosquito does not live a day and a fly does not live a year. A folk saying about a mosquito angry for seven years is explained as using mosquito-years. Next, רב הונא teaches that an extra or missing back leg makes an animal a טרפה, because an extra limb counts like a missing one. The גמרא applies this to extra organs: two ceca, unusual tubes between the stomachs, and a double intestine. In each case it asks whether the extra part is a defect or just normal anatomy. רבי יוחנן then links רבי יהודה's ruling on a bird whose down was removed with רבי ישמעאל's ruling on פיגול, and רבא pushes back. A new משנה teaches that sick animals are still כשרה, while poison deadly to people makes the meat forbidden because of סכנת נפשות. The amud ends with the גמרא asking what תיעה is, and רב יהודה's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Dates stored in a jar for twelve months are permitted
steps.stepSummary: Dates kept in a jar for twelve months are permitted, even if worms are found in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: These dates that sit in a jar are permitted after twelve months of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling: dates stored in a jar become permitted once twelve months have passed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on the idea that a creature without bones cannot live a full year. So any worm found after twelve months could not have been there since the dates were picked. It must have formed later, inside the jar, and that kind of worm is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The dates are not permitted because worms are fine to eat. They are permitted because any worm found must have formed after the dates were picked, and that kind of worm is allowed.

phrases.english: These dates of the jar
after twelve months of the year are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier idea that boneless creatures do not live a full year to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dates stored in a jar for twelve months are permitted.

steps.title: Mosquitoes and flies have short lives
steps.stepSummary: רב says no mosquito lives a full day and no fly lives a full year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: There is no mosquito that is one day old, and there is no fly that is one year old.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a statement about how short the lives of these small creatures are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the idea from step 1 that small boneless creatures do not last long. A mosquito does not survive even one day, and a fly does not survive a whole year.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֵית בָּקָא בַּר יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: Rav said: There is no mosquito one day old,
and there is no fly one year old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֵית בָּקָא בַּר יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea about short-lived creatures behind step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mosquito does not live a full day, and a fly does not live a full year.

steps.title: A folk saying about a mosquito angry for seven years
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רב with a popular saying in which a female mosquito stays angry at the male for seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But people say, 'The female mosquito rebelled against the male mosquito for seven years.' She said to him: 'I saw a man from מחוזא bathing in the water. He came out and wrapped himself in sheets. You sat on him and sucked blood from him, and you did not tell me!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רב's statement using a popular saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mosquito can stay angry for seven years, it seems mosquitoes live for years, not less than a day. That would go against רב in step 2.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But don't people say:
Seven years the female mosquito rebelled against the male mosquito.
For she said to him:
I saw a man from Meḥoza
who was bathing in the water,
and he came up and wrapped himself in sheets,
and you sat on him and sucked from him,
phrases.notes: He means the male sucked the man's blood.

phrases.english: and you did not let me know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that a mosquito does not live a full day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A saying about a mosquito staying angry for seven years suggests that mosquitoes live for years.

steps.title: The saying speaks in the mosquito's own measures
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that folk sayings about mosquitoes use the mosquito's own scale, just like the saying about a mosquito's huge striking weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: By your logic, what about the saying people have, 'Sixty מנה of iron hang on the mosquito's hammer'? Is that really possible? How much does the mosquito itself weigh? Rather, it means their own מנה. Here too, it means their own years.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב by showing that these sayings cannot be taken literally in human terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one thinks a tiny mosquito carries huge weights of iron. That saying must mean weights on a mosquito's tiny scale. In the same way, 'seven years' means seven mosquito-years, which are very short. So רב's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning the challenger's logic back on him)
A weight or coin equal to 100 dinars
A hammer or mallet (here, the mosquito's sting)

steps.whatToRemember: Folk sayings about tiny creatures speak in the creature's own scale. So רב's rule stays: mosquitoes and flies are very short-lived.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
that which people say:
"Sixty maneh of iron
phrases.notes: A maneh is 100 dinars, so this comes to six thousand dinars of iron.

phrases.english: hang on the mosquito's hammer",
is there such a thing?
How much is it itself?
phrases.notes: How much can a tiny mosquito weigh in the first place?

phrases.english: Rather, it means in their own maneh;
here too, it means in their own years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source using a parallel saying
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The saying speaks of seven human years, so mosquitoes would live a long time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The saying speaks of mosquito-years. Mosquitoes really live less than a day.

steps.title: A משנה: five legs or three legs is a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from בכורות: an animal with five legs, or with only three, has a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: An animal that has five legs, or that has only three, has a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about animals with an extra or missing leg. This sets up רב הונא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מום means the animal is not fit to be brought as a קרבן. The משנה only says it is a מום. It does not say whether the animal is also a טרפה, which would make it forbidden to eat. That open question is what רב הונא will address.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that makes an animal unfit to be a קרבן

phrases.english: We learned there:
An animal with five legs,
or that has only three –
this is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the mosquito discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal with five legs or three legs has a מום.

steps.title: רב הונא: a back leg also makes it a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the משנה is talking about front legs. An extra or missing back leg makes the animal a טרפה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They taught this only when the extra or missing leg is a front leg. But if the extra or missing leg is a back leg, the animal is also a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows the משנה. He explains which case it is talking about and adds a stricter rule for the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the front-leg case the animal has a מום, but it is not a טרפה. In the back-leg case it has a מום and is also a טרפה, so it is forbidden to eat. The word נמי ("also") shows that the back-leg case still counts as a מום. It simply adds the טרפה status on top.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (limits a ruling)
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Here יד does not mean a human hand. It means the animal's front leg, and רגל means its back leg.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָסֵר וְיָתֵר בַּיָּד,
phrases.english: They taught this only where it was missing or extra in the foreleg,
but if it was missing or extra in the hind leg –
it is also a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָסֵר וְיָתֵר בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra or missing front leg is only a מום. An extra or missing back leg is a מום and also a טרפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the משנה from the laws of קרבנות into the laws of טרפות. That makes it relevant to whether such an animal may be eaten.

steps.title: Why would an extra leg make it a טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב הונא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why an extra back leg would make the animal a טרפה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A missing back leg as a טרפה is easy to understand. But it is surprising that having more legs could also make the animal a טרפה. The question is aimed mainly at the extra-leg case.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an extra back leg makes an animal a טרפה.

steps.title: An extra limb counts like a missing one
steps.stepSummary: Any extra limb is treated as if a limb were removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any extra limb is considered like a removed one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an extra limb is treated the same as a missing limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal whose back leg was removed is a טרפה. Since an extra limb counts like a removed one, an extra back leg also makes the animal a טרפה. A removed front leg does not make it a טרפה, so an extra front leg is only a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra limb counts as a removed limb
Is considered like, is compared to

steps.whatToRemember: The rule יתר כנטול: an extra limb is treated like a missing limb. This is why an extra back leg makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule can be used for other extra body parts in the laws of טרפות.

phrases.english: Any extra is considered like removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An extra limb counts like a removed limb, and a removed back leg makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: An animal with two ceca is ruled a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: An animal had two ceca. רבינא ruled it a טרפה because of רב הונא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an animal that had two ceca. They brought it to רבינא, and he ruled it a טרפה based on רב הונא's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where רבינא puts רב הונא's rule into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא taught that an extra limb counts as if a limb were missing. An animal missing its cecum is a טרפה, so an animal with an extra cecum is a טרפה too.

keyTerms.meaning: The cecum, a pouch-shaped part of the intestines
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: A certain animal
that had two ceca,
they brought it to Ravina,
and he ruled it a tereifa based on Rav Huna.
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's rule from step 8: an extra limb counts like a missing one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא חֵיוְתָא דַּהֲוָה לַהּ תַּרְתֵּי סַנְיָא דֵּיבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב הונא's principle (extra limb = missing limb) to an actual case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal with two ceca is a טרפה, because an extra organ counts like a missing one.

steps.title: If the two ceca connect, the animal is kosher
steps.stepSummary: If the two ceca empty into each other, the animal is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the two of them empty into each other, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבינא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When food can pass freely between the two ceca, they work as one organ. So there is no real extra organ, and the animal is כשרה.

phrases.english: But if they empty into each other –
it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the טרפה ruling of step 9 to ceca that are not connected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two ceca that empty into each other count as one organ, and the animal is כשרה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ceca make the animal a טרפה, unless they empty into each other and work like one organ.

steps.title: A tube from the reticulum to the omasum
steps.stepSummary: An animal had a tube running from the reticulum to the omasum, and רב אשי wanted to rule it a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain tube that went out from the reticulum to the omasum, and רב אשי thought to declare the animal a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new case and gives רב אשי's first thought. This sets up the reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי saw this tube as an extra, unusual organ. Following the idea that extra organs can make an animal a טרפה, he leaned toward ruling it forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The reticulum, one of the stomachs of an animal that chews its cud
The omasum, another of the stomachs
He thought to declare it a טרפה

phrases.english: A certain tube
that went out from the reticulum to the omasum,
Rav Ashi thought to declare it a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא גּוּבְתָּא דַּהֲוָה נָפְקָא מִבֵּי כָסֵי לְהוּבְלִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case of an unusual extra structure, after the ceca case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי's first thought: an extra tube from the reticulum to the omasum makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: Wild animals all have this tube
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא מר בר חייא tells רב אשי that animals out in the fields all have such a tube, so it is normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא מר בר חייא said to רב אשי: All these animals out in the fields have this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא מר בר חייא pushes back on רב אשי's plan to call the animal a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A structure that is common in many animals is not an extra organ. It is just normal anatomy, so the animal stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that live outside, in the fields

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא מָר בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna Mar bar Ḥiyya said to Rav Ashi:
All these animals that live outside
have it this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא מָר בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's thought from step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects calling this specific tube (reticulum to omasum) an extra organ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tube is common in animals that live outside, so it is normal, not a defect.
steps.whyThisMatters: Something that is normal for many animals is not a defect. The next case shows the limits of this idea.

steps.title: A tube from the reticulum to the rumen
steps.stepSummary: A different tube ran from the reticulum to the rumen, and מר בר רב אשי wanted to rule the animal כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain tube that passed from the reticulum to the rumen, and מר בר רב אשי thought to declare the animal kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a similar-looking case and gives מר בר רב אשי's first thought. This sets up רב אושעיא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי wanted to compare this to the previous case, where the tube was declared normal. But this tube connects different stomachs.

keyTerms.meaning: The rumen, the large first stomach

phrases.english: A certain tube
that passed from the reticulum to the rumen,

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַכְשׁוֹרַהּ.
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi thought to declare it kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גּוּבְתָּא דַּהֲוָה מְעַבְּרָא מִבֵּי כָסֵי לִכְרֵסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to stretch the כשרה ruling of step 12 to a different tube.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בר רב אשי's first thought: a tube from the reticulum to the rumen is also normal, so the animal is כשרה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two tubes. Step 11 was reticulum to omasum. This one is reticulum to rumen.

steps.title: Each case only goes as far as what was taught
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says we cannot treat all tubes alike. Only what was explicitly declared normal is normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said to him: Do you think they were all woven in one weave? Where it was said, it was said. Where it was not said, it was not said.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא rejects מר בר רב אשי's comparison, so the animal is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that a tube is normal was said only about the reticulum-to-omasum tube. A tube between other stomachs is not covered, so we cannot call it normal without a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenging question)
They were woven in one weave, meaning they are all the same

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said to him:
Is that to say all of them
were woven in one weave?
phrases.notes: Are all these tubes really the same thing? They are not.

phrases.english: Where it was said – it was said,
where it was not said – it was not said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ בַּחֲדָא מְחִיתָא מַחֵתִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects stretching the ruling about one tube to a different tube.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כשרה ruling was said only about a specific tube. Different anatomy cannot be assumed to be normal.
steps.whatToRemember: An unusual organ is only called normal where that was clearly taught. We do not stretch it to other cases.

steps.title: Two intestines: a טרפה in an animal, כשרה in a bird
steps.stepSummary: נתן בר שילא testified before רבי that an animal with two intestines coming out together is a טרפה, but a bird like this is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: נתן בר שילא, head of the butchers of ציפורי, testified before רבי about two intestines that come out of an animal together: it is a טרפה. The same thing in a bird is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an expert's testimony about another extra-organ case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two intestines in an animal count as an extra organ, so the animal is a טרפה. In birds this is common and normal, so the bird is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The same case in a bird

phrases.english: Natan bar Sheila testified,
the head of the butchers of Tzippori, before Rabbi,
about two intestines
that come out of the animal as one,
phrases.notes: He means they come out of the stomach side by side.

phrases.english: that it is a tereifa,
and the same in a bird – it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד נָתָן בַּר שֵׁילָא רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דְּצִיפּוֹרִי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another extra-organ case, this time from a recorded testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two intestines coming out together make an animal a טרפה, but a bird with this is כשרה.

steps.title: Only when they come out at two separate spots
steps.stepSummary: The טרפה ruling applies only when the intestines come out at two places. If they come out at one spot and join within a fingerbreadth, the animal is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When they come out at two places. But if they come out at one place and join within about a finger's width, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The testimony now limits its own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two intestines from two separate openings are truly an extra organ. If they start at one spot and join into one intestine within a fingerbreadth, they count as one, so the animal is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (introduces a limit)
They end, here meaning they join into one

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When they come out at two places,
but if they come out at one place,
and they end within a finger's width –
phrases.notes: They join into one intestine within about a finger's width.

phrases.english: it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? שֶׁיּוֹצְאִין בִּשְׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the טרפה ruling of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two intestines make an animal a טרפה only if they come out at separate places. If they come out together and join within a fingerbreadth, the animal is כשרה.
steps.whatToRemember: Just like the two ceca in step 10, if the two parts quickly join and work as one, it is not an extra organ, and the animal is כשרה.

steps.title: Two views on when the double intestine is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי and רב אסי argue about the כשרה case from step 16. One says the two intestines must merge back into one tube right away. The other says it is כשרה even if they do not merge right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי and רב אסי disagree about this. One says: it is kosher only if the two intestines come back together and merge. The other says: it is kosher even if they do not merge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between two אמוראים about the kosher case from step 16, where the intestines come out from one spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that intestines coming out from one spot can be כשרה. The question is how soon they must join back into one tube. One view needs them to rejoin right away. The other is more lenient, and step 19 explains how far that leniency goes.

keyTerms.meaning: They come back and merge into one

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rav Ami and Rav Asi disagree about it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the kosher case from the last step, where the two intestines come out from one spot.

phrases.english: One says: it is only where they come back and merge,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי.
phrases.english: and one says: even though they do not come back and merge.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines more exactly the kosher case of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: כשרה only if the intestines rejoin. Other view: כשרה even if they do not rejoin.

steps.title: How does the lenient view explain 'within a fingerbreadth'?
steps.stepSummary: The words 'within a fingerbreadth' fit the view that the intestines must rejoin. But what do those words mean for the view that they don't need to rejoin?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the one who says the intestines must merge again, that explains why it teaches 'within a fingerbreadth.' But for the one who says it is kosher even if they don't merge, what does 'within a fingerbreadth' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second, more lenient view. It asks how that view can explain the words 'within a fingerbreadth.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the strict view, 'within a fingerbreadth' means the two tubes must rejoin within that distance. The lenient view does not require them to rejoin at all, so those words seem to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works well (for one side)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
it is only where they come back and merge,
that is why it teaches "within a fingerbreadth."
phrases.notes: These are the words from the ruling in step 16: they join within a fingerbreadth.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי,
phrases.english: even though they do not come back and merge,
what is "within a fingerbreadth"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הוּא דְּהָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second view of step 17 against the wording of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that it is כשרה even if the intestines do not rejoin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'within a fingerbreadth' seem to describe rejoining, so this view leaves them with no meaning.

steps.title: The fingerbreadth is measured at the lower end
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view answers that 'within a fingerbreadth' is measured at the lower end. The tubes only need to join before the last fingerbreadth at the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means within a fingerbreadth, measured from below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question for the lenient view. The fingerbreadth is measured at the bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the lenient view, 'they end within a fingerbreadth' is measured from the bottom end of the intestines. The two tubes do not have to merge right away. It is enough if they join before the last fingerbreadth at the lower end. This way the wording fits both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: From below, at the lower end

phrases.english: Within a fingerbreadth from below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Within a fingerbreadth' means the two tubes must rejoin.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Within a fingerbreadth' is measured from the lower end. The tubes only need to join before the last fingerbreadth, so both views fit the wording.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב אמי and רב אסי can explain 'within a fingerbreadth.' One needs the intestines to join back together soon after they come out. The other allows it as long as they join before the last fingerbreadth at the lower end.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a bird whose down was removed is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי יהודה says that if a bird's down was removed, it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the down was removed, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה to set up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats a bird's soft down like an animal's skin. Just as removing the skin makes an animal a טרפה, removing the down makes the bird פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The soft down feathers on a bird's body

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If the down was removed, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם נִיטְּלָה הַנּוֹצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird whose down was removed is פסולה, like an animal whose skin was removed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן links רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל hold the same idea. רבי ישמעאל says the down joins with the meat for the measure of פיגול, which shows he also treats the down like skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל said the same thing. רבי יהודה said what we just quoted. רבי ישמעאל, as we learned: רבי ישמעאל says the down joins together with the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן connects רבי יהודה's ruling to a ruling of רבי ישמעאל from a different area of halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל counts the down together with the meat to make a כזית for פיגול. רבי יוחנן sees this as the same idea as רבי יהודה's: the down is like an animal's skin, a real part of the bird.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins together to complete a measure
A קרבן made invalid by planning to eat it after its time

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yishmael said one thing.
Rabbi Yehuda: that which we said;
Rabbi Yishmael: as we learned:
Rabbi Yishmael says: the down joins together.
phrases.notes: The down joins with the bird's meat to add up to a כזית for the laws of פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רבי יהודה's ruling from step 20 to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה (טרפה) and רבי ישמעאל (פיגול) both treat the down like an animal's skin.

steps.title: רבא: each ruling may be only about its own topic
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the two may not agree. רבי יהודה may only mean טרפה, because without its down the bird has no protection, and for פיגול he may hold like the רבנן. רבי ישמעאל may only mean פיגול, but for טרפה he may hold that the down does not protect the bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: maybe that is not so. רבי יהודה only said this about טרפה, because the bird has nothing else to protect it. But about פיגול, he holds like the רבנן. And רבי ישמעאל only said his ruling about פיגול. But about טרפה, the down does not protect the bird.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבי יוחנן. He shows that each sage's ruling could be limited to his own topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's reason is protection: a bird with no down is in danger, and that only matters for טרפה. רבי ישמעאל's ruling is about counting the down for פיגול, and that does not mean he thinks the down protects the bird. So the two rulings do not prove one shared idea.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said it (in this case), not more
An animal or bird with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
The Sages who argue with him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל agree that the down is like skin. רבא says each may only have meant his own topic: רבי יהודה for טרפה and רבי ישמעאל for פיגול.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying either ruling is wrong. He is only saying the two rulings don't prove the two sages agree.

phrases.english: Rava said: perhaps it is not so.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said it here
regarding טרפה,
since there is nothing that protects it;
but regarding becoming פיגול,
he holds like the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָתָם
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael only said it there
regarding becoming פיגול;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן טְרֵפָה – אַגּוֹנֵי לָא מַגֵּין.
phrases.english: but regarding טרפה, it does not protect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן's linking in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the two sages agree, not their separate rulings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each ruling may rest on a reason that belongs to its own topic: protection for טרפה, and counting the down as part of the bird for פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that two rulings that look alike are not the same idea if their reasons are different.

steps.title: The משנה: harmful foods, deadly poison, and snake bites
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists sick animals, and animals that ate harmful things, that are still כשרה. If the animal ate deadly poison or was bitten by a snake, it is not a טרפה, but it is forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An animal that is congested with blood, that suffered from smoke, that was chilled, that ate oleander, that ate chicken droppings, or that drank bad water is kosher. If it ate deadly poison or a snake bit it, it is permitted as far as טרפה goes, but forbidden because of danger to life.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists animals that are sick or ate harmful things but are still kosher, and then two cases that are forbidden for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick animal is not automatically a טרפה. טרפה means a specific kind of fatal damage to the body. Deadly poison and snake venom don't make the animal a טרפה, but the poison can harm the person who eats the meat, so it is forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal overcome by too much blood (congested)
An animal with a fatal defect that makes it forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of forbidden. Deadly poison does not make the animal a טרפה. It is forbidden only because eating it could hurt the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya tests this משנה's two categories: still כשרה, versus permitted as far as טרפה but forbidden for safety.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An animal congested with blood, or one that suffered from smoke,
or one that got chilled, or one that ate oleander,
or one that ate chicken droppings,
or one that drank bad water: it is kosher.

phrases.aramaic: אָכְלָה סַם הַמָּוֶת, אוֹ שֶׁהִכִּישָׁהּ נָחָשׁ –
phrases.english: If it ate deadly poison, or a snake bit it,
it is permitted as far as טרפה is concerned,
but it is forbidden because of danger to life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the discussion of a bird's down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sick animals, or ones that ate harmful things, are כשרה. Deadly poison or a snake bite does not make the animal a טרפה, but it is forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.

steps.title: שמואל: an animal fed חלתית is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if an animal was fed חלתית (asafoetida), it is a טרפה, because the sharp plant pokes holes in its intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל says: if one fed it asafoetida, it is a טרפה. Why? Because it makes holes in its intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from שמואל about another food, חלתית, that makes the animal a טרפה. It also gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is different from the משנה's list. Here the food does real physical damage, holes in the intestines, and a hole in the intestines is a classic טרפה. So it is not just a question of sickness or danger.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel says:
If one fed it asafoetida, it is a tereifa.
What is the reason?
Because it pokes holes in its intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case to the topic of the משנה: a food that does make the animal a טרפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal fed חלתית is a טרפה, because the plant pokes holes in its intestines.

steps.title: רב שיזבי's ברייתא clashes with שמואל and with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי quotes a ברייתא that calls an animal fed חלתית kosher, against שמואל. The same ברייתא calls an animal that ate deadly poison kosher, while the משנה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי objects from a ברייתא: An animal congested with blood, one that suffered from smoke, one that ate oleander, one that ate chicken droppings, one that drank bad water, one fed תיעה, asafoetida, or peppers, or one that ate deadly poison is kosher. If a snake or a mad dog bit it, it is permitted as far as טרפה goes, but forbidden because of danger to life. So the two statements about asafoetida clash, and the two statements about deadly poison clash!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict two earlier sources at once: שמואל about חלתית, and the משנה about deadly poison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts חלתית on the kosher list, but שמואל said it makes the animal a טרפה. The ברייתא also puts deadly poison on the kosher list, but the משנה said deadly poison is forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of plant the animal was fed
It is a difficulty; the sources contradict

phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi raises an objection:
An animal congested with blood, or one that suffered from smoke,
or one that ate oleander, or one that ate rooster droppings,
or one that drank bad water,
or one fed tia, asafoetida, or peppers,
or one that ate deadly poison: it is kosher.

phrases.aramaic: הִכִּישָׁהּ נָחָשׁ, אוֹ שֶׁנְּשָׁכָהּ כֶּלֶב שׁוֹטֶה –
phrases.english: If a snake bit it, or a mad dog bit it,

phrases.aramaic: מוּתֶּרֶת מִשּׁוּם טְרֵפָה, וַאֲסוּרָה מִשּׁוּם סַכָּנַת נְפָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: it is permitted as far as tereifa goes, but forbidden because of danger to life.
So asafoetida contradicts asafoetida,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא says חלתית is kosher; שמואל said it makes a טרפה.

phrases.english: and deadly poison contradicts deadly poison!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא says it's kosher; our משנה said it's forbidden because of danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling (step 24) and the משנה (step 23) from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling on חלתית, and the משנה's ruling on סם המות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists both חלתית and deadly poison as fully kosher, which goes against both earlier rulings.

steps.title: חלתית: leaves versus sharp slivers
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings on חלתית talk about different forms of the plant. The ברייתא means the leaves, which are kosher. שמואל means the sharp slivers, which make the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two statements about asafoetida don't contradict. Here it means leaves, there it means slivers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different form of חלתית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft leaves don't pierce the intestines, so the ברייתא can call the animal kosher. The hard, sharp slivers do pierce them, so שמואל calls it a טרפה. Both rulings stand.

phrases.english: Asafoetida against asafoetida is not difficult:
here it means leaves, there it means slivers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: each source is talking about a different form of the plant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be talking about the same חלתית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaves are kosher (the ברייתא); sharp slivers make the animal a טרפה (שמואל).

steps.title: Deadly poison: deadly to the animal versus deadly to a person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means poison that is deadly only to the animal, so the meat is safe and kosher. The משנה means poison that is deadly to people, so the meat is forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two statements about deadly poison don't contradict. This one is poison deadly to the animal itself; that one is poison deadly to a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction by explaining that 'deadly poison' means two different things in the two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the poison only kills animals, the person who eats the meat is in no danger, so the ברייתא allows it. If the poison kills people, eating the meat is dangerous, so the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its own; poison deadly to the animal itself
Of a person; poison deadly to a human

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are solved by splitting the cases. Leaves are not slivers, and poison deadly to animals is not poison deadly to people.

phrases.aramaic: סַם הַמָּוֶת אַסַּם הַמָּוֶת לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Deadly poison against deadly poison is not difficult:
this one is deadly to the animal itself, that one is deadly to a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַם הַמָּוֶת אַסַּם הַמָּוֶת לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: two kinds of poison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Deadly poison' seemed to mean the same thing in both sources.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means poison deadly to the animal, so it is kosher. The משנה means poison deadly to people, so it is forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.

steps.title: Isn't animal poison the same as הרדופני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the ברייתא's deadly poison is poison for animals, isn't that just הרדופני? The ברייתא already listed that separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't poison deadly to an animal the same as oleander?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave, which now seems to make the ברייתא repeat itself. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הרדופני is a plant that is poisonous to animals, and the ברייתא already listed it. If 'deadly poison' also means animal poison, why list it again?

phrases.english: Poison deadly to an animal: isn't that oleander?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer in step 27, because that answer makes the ברייתא look repetitive.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the ברייתא list both הרדופני and animal poison, if they are the same thing?

steps.title: There are two kinds of animal poison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are two different kinds of poison deadly to animals. הרדופני is one, and the ברייתא's 'deadly poison' is another.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of deadly poison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the ברייתא is not repeating itself, because it lists two different poisons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since הרדופני and the other animal poison are separate things, the ברייתא needed to mention both. So the answer from step 27 still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Bottom line: poison deadly only to animals, including הרדופני, leaves the animal kosher. Poison deadly to people makes the meat forbidden because of סכנת נפשות.

phrases.english: There are two kinds of deadly poison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הרדופני and the other animal poison are two different poisons, so the ברייתא lists both.

steps.title: What is תיעה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word תיעה in the ברייתא means, and רב יהודה starts to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is תיעה? רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word תיעה means. It is setting up the next move: רב יהודה's explanation, which comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said an animal that was fed תיעה is still kosher, but it never said what תיעה is. Now that the גמרא has finished settling the questions about חלתית and deadly poison, it goes back to explain this unclear word. This is a question about the meaning of a word. It is not a challenge to anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: What? This is the word the גמרא uses to ask for the meaning of a word or idea.
A plant or substance named in the ברייתא. An animal fed it stays kosher. Its exact identity is what the גמרא is asking about.
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is attacking the ברייתא here. It is only asking what a word means, and the answer starts in the next line.

phrases.english: What is tia?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא from Step 25, which said an animal fed תיעה is kosher.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the questions about the ברייתא are settled in Steps 26-29, the גמרא turns to explain a different unclear word in that same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the substance called תיעה, which the ברייתא says leaves an animal kosher?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is given by רב יהודה. His words continue in the next part of the daf.
